intro.lede: Work is changing too fast to figure out alone. So we don't. The Upskilling Labs is a free community of people near you, figuring it out together, in person.
intro.terms: Join once, and three paths open up.
intro.note: Creates your free Upskilling account, with Google. Everything after that, from workshops to applying for a Build Cycle, happens inside it.
intro.$people: The faces are the Inaugural AI Cohort's portraits (OLOS public/assets/cohort-grid-sample.png); the count is the DC Lab's on Sep 29, 2026. In OLOS, both from its members.
intro.label: What this is

items.title: Free, always.
items.body: Workshops, Build Cycles and everything we make cost nothing.

items.title: Twice a week, at the library.
items.body: Drop-in workshops in person at DC Public Library, with some online.

items.title: No tech background.
items.body: Just a willingness to learn by doing, alongside others.

items.title: Built by the people who learn here.
items.body: Contributors improve the workshops, the Build Cycle and the tools, in the open, for every Lab that comes next.

threads.$comment: Joining is the one action; it opens three paths that weave together. In the world (src/scripts/orbnet.ts) the paths are three of the orb's orbits, in the same dust, which unwind into one braid hanging from the orb; each chapter draws its own strand in to a single thread; then the braid again, then the orbits. They aren't steps: most people do all three, in their own order. `then` is what each path's way in says at the close.
threads.title: Learn it. Build it. Pass it on.
threads.lede: They aren't steps. They're threads: what you learn goes into what you build, and what you build goes back to everyone.
threads.alt: Three of the orb's orbits unwinding into one braid of three strands: teal, red and silver.

items.name: Pass it on
items.then: Your account, then a place to start.

chapters.$comment: The three paths, one scene each in the journey: the world's weave draws in to that path's thread, and the words sit beside it. Each links down to its detail after the journey. No levels, pins, membership or dues here.

learn.title: Get sharp, in good company.
learn.lede: Workshops in person at DC Public Library, some online, on the skills work runs on now. No application, no prerequisites. Anyone can come.

build.title: Make something real.
build.lede: A Build Cycle: find your Pod around a problem situation, form a team of three to five, and build it together, with Mentors beside you, all the way to the Showcase.

give.title: Make it better for the next person.
give.lede: The workshops and the Build Cycle are how a group builds expertise that keeps up with change, and turns it into new ideas. Contributors make them better, in the open, so every Lab that comes next starts ahead.
give.heading: Start where you're useful.

ways.title: Mentor.
ways.body: Be the person in the room who's done it before, there when a Pod gets stuck. A single workshop, or a whole cycle.

ways.title: Improve how it works.
ways.body: We run the Build Cycle on ourselves. Try something new in a workshop or a cycle, see what it does, and turn what works into a playbook any Lab can use.

ways.title: Build the tools.
ways.body: The platform The Labs runs on is open source. Code, design and writing are all welcome.

learn.label: Learn what's next
learn.note: Your free account, then a workshop.

give.label: Share what I know
give.note: Your free account, then a place to start.

together.$comment: The weave again, after the three threads: the paths back together, then the system.
together.title: Each one makes the others stronger.
together.lede: Most people end up doing all three. Every cycle, the people who learned here become the people the next ones learn from.

how.title: From a workshop to the Showcase.

steps.title: Create your account.
steps.body: Free, with Google. Everything else happens inside it: events, Slack, your profile, and applying.

steps.title: Drop into a workshop.
steps.body: Twice a week at the library, some online. Anyone can come; most people start here.

steps.title: Apply for a Build Cycle.
steps.body: Places are limited. Twelve weeks: heaviest at the start and the end, steady in between.

steps.title: Find your Pod.
steps.body: Month one: Pods of nine or more form around a problem situation. Everyone lands in one.

steps.title: Build with your team.
steps.body: Teams of three to five form around the projects you propose, with Mentors beside you.

steps.title: Show it. Pass it on.
steps.body: Show what you built at the Showcase, in public and open source. Then mentor, run a Pod, or bring the next person in.

how.markButton: Your Upskiller button, new this cycle

honest.$comment: A realistic preview, before anyone commits: some people deciding it isn't for them is the point. The application itself, its dates, its questions and who to ask live inside the account (OLOS), not on the public pages.
honest.title: What it is, and what it isn't.

items.title: No lectures.
items.body: Workshops teach skills, your Pod is where you practise, Mentors help when you're stuck, and you teach what you learn.

items.title: Not job placement.
items.body: You leave with credited open-source work, an audience at the Showcase, and people who've built with you.

items.title: In person.
items.body: Evenings at the library in DC, with some sessions online. Being in the room is most of it.

items.title: A real commitment.
items.body: Twelve weeks. Month one, while Pods form, and the run-up to the Showcase are the heaviest; the middle is steady. Most people feel unsure while Pods form, and everyone lands in one.

cycle.$comment: Two states, switched by date on the page itself so it never goes stale: open until `closes`, then underway. `closes` is the kickoff date until the deadline is set. In OLOS, from the cycle's own dates.
cycle.title: Fall 2026 starts October 13.
cycle.body: Twelve weeks, a Pod of curious peers, and a problem worth solving. Places are limited. It's an open cycle: the projects are open source, free for anyone to use and build on.
cycle.apply: Create your account, then apply from inside it.

closed.title: The next cycle is coming.
